newsitem.title: DENMARK: POLL - Bigger Danish May c/a, trade surpluses seen.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Bigger Danish May c/a, trade surpluses seen.

text.p: Eight economists polled by Reuters in a survey issued on Monday forecast solid increases in Denmark's May foreign trade and current account surpluses.
The panel predicted an average 2.6 billion crown seasonally adjusted foreign trade surplus, excluding ships, for May, with estimates in the +2.0 to +3.0 billion crown range.
As regards May's current account, the economists forecast an average surplus of 1.2 billion crowns, with predictions ranging from -0.3 to +3.1 billion crowns.
In April, Denmark's seasonally adjusted foreign trade surplus excluding ships was 1.5 billion crowns, with the current account surplus at 0.1 billion crowns.

"Due to rising pork prices, farm exports are expected to help the foreign trade surplus up in May, while lower interest repayments on foreign debt should mean a bigger current account surplus," one economist said.
The Danish national statistics office issues its May foreign trade and current account data on Wednesday August 6 at 0730 GMT.
